title: Patterns

parent.learn: A pattern has a part that repeats.
parent.why: In 🔴🔵🔴🔵 the part “🔴🔵” repeats. Once you find that part, you know what comes next — that is predicting, the heart of maths.

parent.learn: Say the pattern aloud: “red, blue, red, blue…”.
parent.why: Hearing the rhythm makes the repeating part easy to notice, especially before the child can read.
Here the same amount (2) is added each time. Skip counting like this makes adding and tables quicker later.

parent.learn: Make your own patterns with beads, blocks or claps.
parent.why: Making a pattern shows the child really understands the rule, not just spotting it.

ask: Clap, clap, stamp, clap, clap, stamp — what comes next?
Make a pattern with spoons and forks.
Find a pattern on your clothes, the floor tiles or a curtain.
Count in twos: 2, 4, 6 … how far can you go?
Red, red, blue, red, red, blue — what comes next?

rounds.h: Red, blue, red, blue… after red comes blue.
Apple, banana, apple, banana… after banana comes apple.
Star, star, moon repeats. After two stars comes the moon.
Dog, cat, dog, cat… next is dog.
Red, yellow, red, yellow… next is red.
Triangle, triangle, circle repeats. After one triangle comes another triangle.
Strawberry, kiwi, strawberry, kiwi… the gap is a kiwi.

rounds.t: Clap, clap, stamp… what comes next?
rounds.h: The pattern is clap, clap, stamp. After one clap comes the second clap.

rounds.t: What comes next? A, B, A, B, A, ___
rounds.h: A, B repeats. After A comes B.
Each number is 2 more than the one before: 8 + 2 = 10.
Full, full, dark repeats. After two full moons comes a dark one.
